lessons.name: Semantic HTML
lessons.desc: Using the right element for meaning: header, nav, main, article, section, aside, footer.
lessons.q: Why does semantic HTML matter? What do you lose by building everything with divs?
lessons.qsub: Which elements would you use to mark up a blog post page, and why?
terms: Aisa tag jiska naam hi uska matlab batata hai — <nav>, <main>, <article>.
Page ka bada hissa jise screen reader user seedha jump karke pahunch sakta hai.
Sab kuch <div> mein likhna — browser aur assistive tech ko kuch samajh nahi aata.
lessons.what:
Definition: Semantic HTML ka matlab hai content ke meaning ke hisaab se tag chunna, dikhne ke hisaab se nahi. Navigation ke liye <nav>, mukhya content ke liye <main>, standalone post ke liye <article>.

Styling CSS ka kaam hai; tag ka kaam hai batana ki ye cheez hai kya.
lessons.analogy: Kitaab ke chapter, heading aur index. Agar sab kuch ek hi bada paragraph ho to koi bhi navigate nahi kar sakta. Semantic tags kitaab ka index hain.
lessons.why: Screen reader, search engine crawler aur reader mode sab tag ke meaning se page samajhte hain. <button> ko free mein keyboard (Enter/Space) aur focus milta hai; <div onclick> ko ye sab haath se banana padta hai — aur aksar bhool jaate hain.
lessons.code:
...
...
...

Title

...
Related links
...
where: <article> + heading hierarchy se SEO aur reader mode dono sahi chalte hain.
<main>, <nav>, <button> se keyboard + screen reader support almost free milta hai.
pros: Accessibility aur SEO bina extra kaam ke behtar
Code padhne mein saaf — tag dekh ke hi structure samajh aata hai
cons: Naye developer ko kab <section> aur kab <div> ka confusion hota hai
gotchas: <section> bina heading ke almost hamesha galat choice hai — styling hook chahiye to <div> use karo
Ek page par ek hi <main> hona chahiye
Heading levels skip mat karo (h1 → h4) — sirf size ke liye heading chunna galat hai, size CSS se badlo

lessons.name: Document Structure & Metadata
lessons.desc: doctype, html lang, head vs body, meta charset, viewport, title, link/script placement.
lessons.q: Walk me through the essential contents of a <head>. Why does the viewport meta tag matter?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between placing a <script> in head vs end of body vs using defer?
terms: <!doctype html> — browser ko batata hai standards mode mein render karo, quirks mode mein nahi.
Mobile browser ko batata hai ki page ko device width par dikhao, zoomed-out desktop layout par nahi.
Text kis encoding mein hai — utf-8 hamesha.
lessons.what:
Definition: Har HTML page ka skeleton: doctype, <html lang>, <head> (metadata, jo dikhta nahi) aur <body> (jo dikhta hai).

<head> mein charset, viewport, title, stylesheet links aur description rehte hain.
lessons.why: Doctype na ho to browser quirks mode mein chala jata hai aur box model jaisi cheezein purani tarah behave karti hain. Viewport meta na ho to mobile par page chhota-chhota dikhta hai. lang screen reader ko sahi accent chunne deta hai aur translation tools ko hint deta hai.
lessons.code:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <title>My App</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Short page summary" />
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/styles.css" />
</head>
<body>
  ...
  <script src="/app.js" defer></script>
</body>
</html>
where: Ye boilerplate bina exception ke chahiye.
title, description aur Open Graph meta se search aur social previews bante hain.
cons: Boilerplate yaad rakhna padta hai (framework/templates isse handle kar dete hain)
gotchas: user-scalable=no mat lagao — zoom rokna accessibility problem hai
charset pehle 1024 bytes ke andar hona chahiye, warna browser galat guess kar sakta hai
Stylesheet mein, script defer ke saath — warna render block hota hai

lessons.name: Forms & Input Types
lessons.desc: form, label association, input types (email, number, date, etc.), name/value, method/action.
lessons.q: How do you correctly associate a label with an input, and why does it matter?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between GET and POST form submission?
terms: <label for=id> ya label ke andar input — click karne par input focus hota hai aur screen reader naam padhta hai.
Form submit mein field ka key yahi banta hai; bina name ke value jaati hi nahi.
email, number, date — mobile par sahi keyboard aur free validation.
lessons.what:
Definition: <form> user input collect karke server ko bhejta hai (action + method). Har field ka name aur ek <label> hona chahiye.

Sahi type chunne se mobile par sahi keyboard khulta hai aur browser basic validation khud kar deta hai.
lessons.why: Placeholder label ka substitute nahi hai — type karte hi gayab ho jata hai aur screen reader par reliable nahi. Native form ko Enter se submit, autofill, password manager sab free milte hain; custom div-based form mein ye sab tootte hain.
lessons.code:
<form action="/signup" method="post">
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required />

  <label>
    Age
    <input name="age" type="number" min="13" max="120" />
  </label>

  <button type="submit">Create account</button>
</form>
where: type=email, type=password, autocomplete se password manager chalta hai.
GET form se URL mein state aa jati hai — shareable aur back-button friendly.
pros: Sahi type se mobile UX behtar
cons: Native look customize karna thoda mushkil
gotchas: <button> ka default type submit hota hai — form ke andar non-submit button ko type="button" do
Bina name ke field submit mein nahi jata
Sirf placeholder se label ka kaam mat chalao

lessons.name: Native Form Validation
lessons.desc: required, pattern, min/max, type-based validation, :valid/:invalid, Constraint Validation API.
lessons.q: How does native HTML form validation work? When would you override it with JS?
lessons.qsub: How do you style a field based on its validity state without JavaScript?
terms: JS se custom error message set karne ka API; khaali string se error hat jata hai.
Pseudo-class jo user ke interact karne ke baad hi invalid state dikhata hai (page load par nahi).
lessons.what:
Definition: HTML attributes se hi validation ho sakti hai: required, minlength, pattern, min/max, type=email. Browser submit rok deta hai aur error bubble dikhata hai.

JS ke liye form.checkValidity(), reportValidity() aur input.validity object milte hain.
lessons.why: Zyada tar basic validation ke liye library ki zarurat nahi. Lekin client validation sirf UX ke liye hai — server par validation hamesha dobara karni padti hai kyunki user DevTools se sab bypass kar sakta hai.
lessons.code:
<input name="zip" required pattern="[0-9]{6}" title="6 digit PIN code" />

<style>
  input:user-invalid { border-color: crimson; }
</style>

<script>
  const form = document.querySelector('form');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (e) => {
    if (!form.checkValidity()) {
      e.preventDefault();
      form.reportValidity();
    }
  });
</script>
where: Required + pattern + type se zyada tar field cover ho jate hain.
setCustomValidity se 'passwords match' jaisi cross-field rule.
pros: Zero JS ke saath kaam karta hai
Accessible aur localized error messages free
cons: Error bubble ka style limited hai
Complex cross-field logic ke liye JS chahiye
gotchas: Client validation security nahi hai — server par dobara validate karo
:invalid page load par hi laal dikha deta hai; :user-invalid ya touched-state use karo
novalidate lagane par native validation band ho jati hai

lessons.name: Images & Media (img, picture, srcset, video)
lessons.desc: alt text, responsive images via srcset/sizes, <picture> art direction, lazy loading, video/audio.
lessons.q: How do srcset and sizes work? How would you serve different images to mobile vs desktop?
lessons.qsub: What does loading="lazy" do and what are its caveats?
terms: Image ka text substitute — screen reader aur image fail hone par dikhta hai. Decorative image ke liye alt="".
Browser ko multiple image sizes dena taaki wo screen aur DPR ke hisaab se sahi wali chune.
Art direction — alag screen par alag crop ya format (AVIF/WebP) dikhane ke liye.
lessons.what:
Definition: <img> ke saath alt, width/height, loading="lazy" hamesha do. Responsive ke liye srcset + sizes; alag crop/format ke liye <picture>.

<video> / <audio> mein controls, preload aur captions (<track>) dena chahiye.
lessons.why: Images page ka sabse bhaari hissa hote hain. Mobile ko 2000px ki image bhejna bandwidth ki barbadi hai. Width/height na dene par image load hote hi layout shift hota hai (CLS kharab).
where: srcset + sizes se mobile data bachta hai.
loading=lazy se initial load halka rehta hai.
pros: Browser khud best candidate chun leta hai
cons: sizes sahi likhna tricky hai — galat sizes se badi image download hoti hai
gotchas: LCP (hero) image par loading=lazy mat lagao
Width/height ya aspect-ratio do, warna layout shift
Alt text mein 'image of...' mat likho; kaam batao

lessons.name: Accessibility Roles & ARIA
lessons.desc: Semantic-first accessibility, ARIA roles/states/properties, when ARIA is needed vs harmful, focus management.
lessons.q: What is the first rule of ARIA? When should you reach for aria-* attributes?
lessons.qsub: How do you make a custom div-based button fully accessible?
terms: Accessibility attributes (role, aria-*) jo assistive tech ko extra meaning dete hain.
Agar native element mil jaye to ARIA mat lagao — <button> > div role=button.
Modal/menu khulne par focus andar le jana aur band hone par wapas lana.
lessons.what:
Definition: Accessibility ka pehla raasta semantic HTML hai. ARIA tab chahiye jab native element se kaam na bane — jaise custom tabs, combobox, live updates (aria-live).

ARIA sirf meaning badalta hai; keyboard behavior aur focus aapko khud banana padta hai.
lessons.why: Galat ARIA, ARIA na hone se bhi bura hai: role="button" laga diya par Enter/Space handle nahi kiya to screen reader user ko button dikhega par chalega nahi. Isliye 'native first, ARIA last'.
lessons.code:
...
3 results found
where: focus trap, aria-modal aur Esc se close; native <dialog> best hai.
aria-live se screen reader ko change announce hota hai.
pros: Custom widgets bhi assistive tech ke liye usable
Icon-only controls ko accessible name milta hai
cons: Galat use se nuksaan; testing screen reader ke saath chahiye
gotchas: aria-hidden="true" focusable element par mat lagao
role behavior nahi deta — keyboard handling khud likhna padta hai
Visible label ho to aria-label ki jagah aria-labelledby/<label> use karo

lessons.name: Script Loading — async vs defer
lessons.desc: Render-blocking scripts, async (load+run ASAP), defer (run after parse, in order), module scripts.
lessons.q: What is the difference between async and defer? Which would you use for a third-party analytics script?
lessons.qsub: Why can a <script> in the <head> hurt First Contentful Paint?
terms: Parser script download + execute hone tak ruk jata hai, page dikhna band.
Parallel download, HTML parse hone ke baad order mein execute.
Parallel download, download hote hi execute — order guarantee nahi.
lessons.what:
Definition: Normal <script> parsing rok deta hai. defer download parallel karta hai aur document parse hone ke baad, order mein run karta hai. async download ke turant baad run karta hai, order ki guarantee nahi.

type="module" scripts by default defer jaise behave karte hain.
lessons.why: Script ke wajah se parser ruke to user ko blank screen dikhti hai (FCP/LCP kharab). Sahi attribute se HTML pehle dikh jata hai aur JS peeche load hota hai.
lessons.code:
<!-- blocks parsing: avoid -->
<script src="app.js"></script>

<!-- app code: order matters, DOM ready ke baad -->
<script src="app.js" defer></script>

<!-- independent third-party (analytics): order ki parwah nahi -->
<script src="analytics.js" async></script>

<script type="module" src="main.js"></script>
where: defer — DOM ready hone par order mein chalta hai.
async — dusre scripts par depend nahi karte.
cons: async scripts ka order unpredictable — dependencies tootti hain
gotchas: Inline script par defer/async ka koi asar nahi
async do dependent scripts par mat lagao
defer script DOMContentLoaded se pehle chalta hai

lessons.name: data-* Attributes & the DOM
lessons.desc: Custom data-* attributes, dataset API, when to use them vs classes or JS state.
lessons.q: What are data-* attributes for? How do you read them in JavaScript?
lessons.qsub: When is a data attribute the wrong tool for holding state?
terms: Custom attribute jo data- se shuru hota hai — HTML mein chhota extra data rakhne ke liye.
JS ya test ke liye element pakadne ka stable tareeka, styling ke liye alag.
lessons.what:
Definition: data-* attributes element par chhota custom data rakhte hain jo JS dataset se padhti hai aur CSS attribute selector ([data-state="open"]) se use kar sakti hai.

Values hamesha string hoti hain.
lessons.why: Server-rendered HTML ko JS se jodne ya state ko CSS tak pahunchane ka simple tareeka hai. Lekin ye sach ka state store nahi — app state ko JS/framework mein rakho.
lessons.code:
<button data-action="delete" data-id="42">Delete</button>

<script>
  document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    const btn = e.target.closest('[data-action="delete"]');
    if (btn) remove(Number(btn.dataset.id)); // string -> number
  });
</script>

<style>
  [data-state="open"] { display: block; }
</style>
where: data-action se ek listener se kai buttons handle hote hain.
data-state/data-theme se CSS ko bina class ke toggle karna.
pros: Markup mein hi context, extra lookup nahi
CSS aur JS dono use kar sakte hain
cons: Values string hoti hain; bada data rakhna galat hai
gotchas: Sensitive data data-* mein mat rakho — page source mein dikhta hai
data-user-id → dataset.userId (kebab to camelCase)
Screen reader data-* ko nahi padhta — meaning ke liye ARIA/semantic use karo

units.title: CSS Core — Selectors, Cascade, Box Model

lessons.name: Selectors & Combinators
lessons.desc: Type, class, id, attribute selectors; descendant, child (>), sibling (+, ~) combinators; :is()/:where().
lessons.q: Explain the different CSS combinators with examples. What does :where() add over :is()?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between .a .b and .a > .b?
terms: Selectors ke beech ka relation: space (descendant), > (child), + (next sibling), ~ (later siblings).
Selector list ko chhota karte hain; :where() ki specificity zero hoti hai.
lessons.what:
Definition: Selector batata hai ki rule kin elements par lagega. Type (p), class (.card), id (#nav), attribute ([href^="https"]) aur combinators se aap precise target kar sakte ho.

:is() aur :where() repeated selectors ko compress karte hain.
lessons.why: Selector jitna simple aur flat, CSS utna maintainable aur fast. Lambe descendant chains (.a .b .c .d) HTML structure se chipak jate hain — structure badla to style tootti hai.
where: h2 + p, article > p jaise structural rules prose ke liye.
pros: Precise targeting bina extra classes ke
cons: Deep chains fragile aur specificity badhate hain
gotchas: :is() ki specificity uske sabse specific argument ke barabar hoti hai, :where() ki zero
Universal * aur bahut deep selectors se bachna
~ sirf baad ke siblings ko match karta hai, pehle wale ko nahi

lessons.name: Specificity & the Cascade
lessons.desc: How the browser resolves conflicting rules: specificity (id > class > type), source order, importance.
lessons.q: How is CSS specificity calculated? How would you resolve two rules fighting over the same element?
lessons.qsub: Where does !important sit in the cascade, and why is it a code smell?
terms: Selector ka weight — inline > id > class/attr/pseudo-class > type/pseudo-element.
Origin/importance → specificity → source order (baad wala jeetta hai).
Normal cascade ko override karta hai; war ke bina use karna mushkil se hi theek hai.
lessons.what:
Definition: Jab do rules same property par conflict karein to browser pehle importance dekhta hai, phir specificity (ID, class, type ki ginti), aur tie ho to jo rule baad mein likha ho wo jeet jata hai.

Specificity ko (ids, classes, types) triple jaisa socho: #a .b p = (1,1,1).
lessons.why: 'Mera style lag kyun nahi raha?' ka 80% jawab specificity hai. Specificity war (!important ke upar !important) se bachne ke liye low-specificity, flat selectors aur @layer use karo.
where: Low specificity base styles + overrides easy.
@layer ya thoda zyada specific selector se library styles override.
cons: Specificity wars se CSS ugly aur kharab ho jata hai
gotchas: Class selector ko kitna bhi chain karo, ID ko nahi hara sakta (classes ID se kam hain, 11 classes != 1 id)
!important ko !important hi hara sakta hai — chain bad hoti hai
Inline style ko sirf !important hara sakta hai

lessons.name: Inheritance & initial/inherit/unset
lessons.desc: Which properties inherit (color, font) vs not (margin, border); inherit, initial, unset, revert keywords.
lessons.q: Which CSS properties inherit by default and which do not? How do you force inheritance?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between unset and revert?
terms: Parent se child ko jati hai: color, font-*, line-height, visibility.
unset = inherited ho to inherit, warna initial; revert = browser default par wapas.
lessons.what:
Definition: Kuch properties (text se jude hue) child elements ko automatic mil jati hain. Box se jude properties nahi milti.

Keywords: inherit (parent ki value lo), initial (spec default), unset, revert.
lessons.why: Isiliye body par font-family ek baar set karne se poore page par lag jata hai. Aur isiliye button/input par font alag dikhta hai — browser unko default font deta hai, inherit nahi karte; font: inherit likhna padta hai.
where: body par set karke poori site cover.
cons: Kaun si property inherit hoti hai ye yaad rakhna padta hai
gotchas: all: unset display bhi hata deta hai — dhyan se
Percent/em values inherit ke baad computed value inherit hoti hai, original nahi
Custom properties (--x) by default inherit hoti hain

lessons.name: The Box Model & box-sizing
lessons.desc: Content, padding, border, margin; content-box vs border-box; why border-box is the sane default.
lessons.q: Explain the CSS box model. What does box-sizing: border-box change and why do people set it globally?
lessons.qsub: A div has width:200px, padding:20px, border:5px. How wide is it in each box-sizing mode?
terms: Har element 4 layers ka box: content → padding → border → margin.
Default: width sirf content ki; padding + border upar se jodte hain.
width mein padding + border shamil — predictable sizing.
lessons.what:
Definition: Har element ek rectangle hai: content, uske chaaron taraf padding, phir border, phir margin (bahar ki jagah).

box-sizing: border-box mein width: 200px ka matlab pura box 200px, padding/border ke saath.
lessons.why: content-box mein width:100%; padding:20px parent se bahar nikal jata hai (100% + 40px). Isiliye almost har project mein global border-box reset hota hai.
cons: Legacy/third-party CSS content-box assume kar sakti hai
gotchas: Margin box ka hissa nahi hai aur background nahi rangta
width: 100% + padding content-box mein overflow karta hai
inline elements par vertical margin/padding layout ko effect nahi karte

lessons.name: Display: block / inline / inline-block
lessons.desc: How elements flow: block (full width), inline (no box dimensions), inline-block (box + inline flow).
lessons.q: What is the difference between block, inline, and inline-block? Give a use case for each.
lessons.qsub: Why can you not set width/height on a pure inline element?
terms: Poori width leta hai, nayi line se shuru; width/height/margin sab kaam karte hain.
Text ke flow mein; width/height ignore, vertical margin ka layout effect nahi.
Inline ki tarah flow karta hai par block ki tarah width/height leta hai.
lessons.what:
Definition: display decide karta hai element kaise flow karega. div, p block hote hain; span, a inline; inline-block dono ka mix; none element ko hata deta hai (layout se bhi).

Aaj layout ke liye zyada tar flex aur grid use hote hain.
lessons.why: 'Mera span par width kaam nahi kar rahi' ya 'button ke neeche gap aa raha' jaise bugs display model samajhne se hal hote hain. Inline-block ke beech whitespace gap bhi isi ki wajah se aata hai.
where: display:block se descender gap hata dete hain.
cons: inline-block gaps jaisi quirks
gotchas: display:none accessibility tree se bhi hata deta hai; opacity:0 nahi
inline elements par width/height ignore hoti hai
display:none element ko animate/transition nahi kar sakte

lessons.name: Margin Collapsing
lessons.desc: Adjacent vertical margins collapse to the larger value; when it happens and how to prevent it.
lessons.q: What is margin collapsing? Show a case where it surprises developers.
lessons.qsub: How do you stop two vertical margins from collapsing?
terms: Do adjacent vertical margins add nahi hote — bada wala rehta hai.
Block Formatting Context — iske andar margins bahar ke margins ke saath collapse nahi karte.
Child ka top margin parent ke bahar nikal jata hai agar beech mein padding/border na ho.
lessons.what:
Definition: Block elements ke vertical margins jab touch karte hain to jodte nahi, balki bada wala hi lagu hota hai (20px + 30px = 30px).

Ye sirf vertical direction mein, normal block flow mein hota hai. Flex/grid items ke margins collapse nahi karte.
lessons.why: Ye intentional feature hai taaki paragraphs ke beech spacing double na ho. Lekin surprise tab hota hai jab child ka margin-top parent ko bhi neeche dhakel deta hai.
pros: Vertical rhythm double spacing se bachta hai
cons: Surprising behaviour jab layout debug karna ho
gotchas: Horizontal margins kabhi collapse nahi hote
Flex/grid items aur floats ke margins collapse nahi hote
gap margin collapse ki wajah se bachne ka accha tareeka hai

lessons.name: Units — px, em, rem, %, vw/vh, ch
lessons.desc: Absolute vs relative units; em (relative to parent font-size) vs rem (root); viewport and content units.
lessons.q: What is the difference between em and rem? When would you choose each?
lessons.qsub: Why can nested em values compound unexpectedly?
terms: Root (html) font-size ke relative — predictable, accessibility ke liye best.
Current element ke font-size ke relative (padding/margin mein) ya parent ke (font-size mein) — nest karne par compound hota hai.
Viewport width/height ka 1% aur '0' character ki width.
lessons.what:
Definition: Absolute: px. Relative: % (parent), em, rem, viewport units (vw, vh, dvh) aur content units (ch, ex).

Font-size ke liye rem, component-internal spacing ke liye em, borders ke liye px common hai.
lessons.why: User browser mein default font size badhata hai to rem wala layout saath badhta hai; px wala nahi — accessibility fayda. ch se text-width limit (max-width: 65ch) readable line length deti hai.
lessons.code:
html { font-size: 100%; }        /* 16px default, user ka setting respect */
h1   { font-size: 2rem; }        /* 32px */
.btn { font-size: 1rem; padding: 0.5em 1em; } /* button ke saath scale */

.prose { max-width: 65ch; }      /* readable line length */
.hero  { min-height: 100dvh; }   /* mobile address bar friendly */
where: rem for sizes; user settings respect.
em padding se component font-size ke saath scale hota hai.
cons: em nesting mein compound hota hai — confusing
gotchas: html { font-size: 62.5% } trick user preference ko tod sakti hai
em font-size mein parent ka, padding mein khud ka font-size use karta hai
100vh mobile par address bar ke wajah se zyada ho sakta hai

lessons.name: CSS Custom Properties (Variables)
lessons.desc: --var declarations, var() with fallbacks, scoping/cascade, runtime theming, contrast with Sass variables.
lessons.q: How do CSS custom properties differ from Sass variables? Why are they powerful for theming?
lessons.qsub: How would you implement a runtime dark-mode toggle using CSS variables?
terms: --brand: #0a84ff; — apna variable, runtime par change ho sakta hai.
var(--brand, fallback) se value padhna, fallback ke saath.
Variable cascade/inherit hota hai — element par override karo to uske children par lagta hai.
lessons.what:
Definition: CSS custom properties --name se declare hoti hain aur var(--name) se use. Ye normal cascading properties hain isliye selector, media query ya JS se runtime par badli ja sakti hain.

Sass variables compile-time par replace ho jate hain, isliye runtime theming nahi kar sakte.
lessons.why: Dark mode, theme switching aur component-level customization (--card-padding) bina extra CSS ke ho jata hai. JS se ek variable badlo, poora subtree update.
where: Tokens ko :root par rakho, theme par override.
cons: Media queries mein var() use nahi kar sakte (breakpoints ke liye)
gotchas: Invalid value hone par property 'guaranteed-invalid' ho jati hai aur fallback nahi chalta jab tak var() mein fallback na do
Case-sensitive: --Brand aur --brand alag
Animation ke liye @property se type register karna padta hai

lessons.name: Flexbox — Main/Cross Axis
lessons.desc: flex container vs items, main/cross axis, justify-content, align-items, align-content, flex-direction.
lessons.q: Explain the flexbox axes. How do justify-content and align-items differ?
lessons.qsub: How do you vertically and horizontally center a single element with flexbox?
terms: Flex direction ki line (row mein horizontal). justify-content isi par kaam karta hai.
Main ke perpendicular. align-items isi par kaam karta hai.
display:flex wala parent; uske direct children flex items bante hain.
lessons.what:
Definition: Flexbox ek dimension (row ya column) mein items ko align aur space dene ka layout system hai. Container par display:flex lagao; flex-direction main axis tay karta hai.

justify-content = main axis, align-items = cross axis, gap = items ke beech spacing, flex-wrap = naye line mein girna.
lessons.analogy: Bookshelf par kitabein: shelf ek direction mein chalti hai (main axis), kitabon ki unchai align karna cross axis hai.
lessons.why: Navbar, toolbar, card row jaise 1D layouts floats/inline-block se bahut aasan ban jate hain: equal heights, centering, space-between sab ek line mein.
where: gap aur wrap se responsive rows.
cons: 2D layout (rows + columns dono) ke liye grid behtar hai
gotchas: flex-direction: column mein justify/align ka role ulta ho jata hai
Flex items ka default min-width:auto hota hai — lamba text overflow kar sakta hai, min-width:0 do
align-content sirf multi-line (wrap) container par kaam karta hai

lessons.name: flex-grow / shrink / basis
lessons.desc: The flex shorthand; how items distribute free space; flex-basis vs width; flex:1 meaning.
lessons.q: What does flex: 1 expand to and what does it actually do?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between flex-basis and width?
terms: Free space mein se kitna hissa lena hai (ratio).
Space kam ho to kitna sikudna hai.
Grow/shrink se pehle item ki starting size (width se zyada priority).
lessons.what:
Definition: flex: grow shrink basis shorthand hai. flex: 1 = 1 1 0 — barabar hissa. flex: none = na grow na shrink. flex: 0 0 200px = fixed 200px.

Pehle flex-basis se starting size, phir bacha hua (ya kam padha hua) space grow/shrink ratio se baanta jata hai.
lessons.why: Sidebar fixed rakhna aur content ko bacha hua space dena (flex:1) sabse common pattern hai. Shrink samjhe bina items 'chipak' jate hain ya overflow karte hain.
cons: flex-basis vs width ka interaction confusing
gotchas: flex-basis width ko override karta hai (jab auto na ho)
flex:1 ka basis 0 hai, isliye content size ignore hota hai
Lamba word/URL overflow ho to min-width:0 ya overflow-wrap

lessons.name: CSS Grid — Tracks & Placement
lessons.desc: grid-template-columns/rows, fr unit, repeat(), gap, minmax(), auto-fit vs auto-fill.
lessons.q: When would you choose Grid over Flexbox? Explain fr and minmax().
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between auto-fit and auto-fill in repeat()?
terms: Track ki min aur max size — minmax(200px, 1fr).
repeat() ke saath jitne tracks fit hon utne banao; auto-fit khaali tracks collapse kar deta hai.
lessons.what: Definition: CSS Grid 2D layout hai: rows aur columns dono. Container par display:grid aur grid-template-columns/rows se tracks define karo; items khud cells mein lag jate hain. gap tracks ke beech spacing hai.
lessons.why: Responsive card grid ke liye ek line kaafi hai: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr)) — bina media query ke columns ki count screen ke hisaab se badal jati hai.
pros: 2D control; items alignment aur spanning aasan
Media query ke bina responsive grids
cons: Chhote 1D layouts ke liye flex zyada simple
gotchas: fr min-content ke neeche nahi sikud-ta; minmax(0,1fr) use karo overflow rokne ke liye
auto-fit aur auto-fill ka fark tab dikhta hai jab items tracks se kam hon
Implicit rows grid-auto-rows se control hoti hain

lessons.name: Grid Template Areas & Line Placement
lessons.desc: Named grid-template-areas, grid-column/row line placement, spanning, implicit vs explicit grid.
lessons.q: How do grid-template-areas work? When are they clearer than line-based placement?
lessons.qsub: What is the implicit grid and how does grid-auto-flow affect it?
terms: Layout ko ASCII-art jaisa naam dena — padhne mein aasan.
grid-column: 1 / 3 — line numbers se item ko span karana.
Jo tracks aapne define nahi kiye par content ke wajah se bane.
lessons.what:
Definition: grid-template-areas se layout ko naam diye jate hain, aur item par grid-area: name lagate hain. Alternatively line numbers/span se placement: grid-column: 1 / span 2.

Explicit grid wo hai jo template mein likha; baaki extra items implicit tracks mein jate hain.
lessons.why: Page layouts (header, sidebar, main, footer) ko media query mein sirf template string badalke reorder kar sakte ho — HTML order nahi chhedna padta.
cons: Visual order aur DOM order alag ho to keyboard/screen reader confusion
gotchas: Areas rectangular honi chahiye — L-shape allowed nahi
Visual reorder se tab order nahi badalta (a11y)
Line numbers 1 se shuru hote hain, tracks se ek zyada

lessons.name: Positioning — static/relative/absolute/fixed/sticky
lessons.desc: Normal flow vs positioned; containing block; offsets; sticky = relative until threshold then fixed.
lessons.q: Explain each position value. What is the containing block for an absolutely positioned element?
lessons.qsub: How does position: sticky decide when to stick, and why does it sometimes silently not work?
terms: Absolute element ka reference — nearest positioned ancestor (relative/absolute/fixed/sticky).
Relative jaisa chalta hai jab tak scroll threshold na aaye, phir fixed jaisa chipak jata hai.
top/right/bottom/left — sirf positioned elements par kaam karte hain.
lessons.what: Definition: static (default, normal flow), relative (apni jagah se offset, space reserve rehta hai), absolute (flow se bahar, nearest positioned ancestor ke hisaab se), fixed (viewport ke hisaab se), sticky (scroll par chipakta hai).
lessons.why: Badges, tooltips, dropdowns aur sticky headers sab positioning se bante hain. 'Absolute element galat jagah dikh raha' ka kaaran aksar parent par position: relative na hona hai.
pros: sticky se JS ki zarurat nahi
cons: Absolute elements flow se bahar — parent ki height collapse ho jati hai
gotchas: Parent par overflow: hidden/auto ho to sticky kaam nahi karta
transform wala ancestor fixed element ka containing block ban jata hai
top sticky ke liye zaroori hai, warna wo kabhi chipakta nahi

lessons.name: z-index & Stacking Contexts
lessons.desc: What creates a stacking context (position+z-index, opacity, transform), why z-index:9999 can fail.
lessons.q: Why can a z-index: 9999 element still appear behind another? Explain stacking contexts.
lessons.qsub: Name three properties (other than z-index) that create a new stacking context.
terms: Ek isolated layer group — iske andar ke z-index sirf andar ke liye matter karte hain.
Positioned/flex/grid items ki layer order; sirf apne stacking context ke andar compare hota hai.
isolation: isolate bina side-effect ke naya stacking context banata hai.
lessons.what:
Definition: Naya stacking context banta hai jab: root element, position + z-index (auto nahi), opacity < 1, transform, filter, isolation:isolate, aur kai aur cases mein.

Do alag contexts ke elements ki comparison parent contexts ke z-index se hoti hai, children ke z-index se nahi.
lessons.why: z-index: 9999 isliye fail hota hai ki aapka element ek aise parent mein hai jo khud ek neeche wale stacking context mein hai. Fix: stacking context ko samjho, z-index badhane se kuch nahi hoga.
where: portal se body ke direct child banana — context issues bachte hain.
pros: Components ko apne andar z-index manage karne dete hain
cons: Hidden contexts (transform, opacity) debug karna mushkil
gotchas: opacity:0.99 ya transform bhi stacking context bana deta hai
z-index static elements par kaam nahi karta (flex/grid items par karta hai)
Modal ko DOM mein bahut andar render mat karo; portal use karo

lessons.name: Centering Techniques
lessons.desc: Flex/grid centering, margin auto, absolute + transform, when each applies.
lessons.q: Give me three ways to center a box both horizontally and vertically. Trade-offs of each?
lessons.qsub: How do you center an element of unknown width and height?
terms: Block ko horizontally center karta hai jab width set ho.
lessons.what: Definition: Context ke hisaab se centering: text ke liye text-align:center; fixed-width block ke liye margin-inline:auto; dono axis ke liye flex ya grid; overlay ke liye position:absolute + inset:0; margin:auto.
lessons.why: Ye sabse common interview sawaal hai. Aaj ka jawab: display:grid; place-items:center. Purane tareeke (absolute + negative margin, table-cell) sirf legacy code mein milte hain.
cons: Context-dependent — ek hi tareeka sab jagah nahi chalta
gotchas: Parent ko height do (min-height) warna vertical centering dikhegi hi nahi
margin: auto ko width chahiye block par horizontal centering ke liye
Absolute + transform tareeka blurry text de sakta hai

lessons.name: Float & Clear (legacy)
lessons.desc: Historical layout with floats, clearfix hack, why floats caused collapsing parents.
lessons.q: What were floats originally for and why did they get abused for layout?
lessons.qsub: What is a clearfix and why was it needed?
terms: Element ko left/right side par hata kar text ko uske around wrap karana.
Hack jo float wale children ke baad parent ko unki height tak khichta hai.
lessons.what:
Definition: float original use text ko image ke around wrap karna tha. 2000s mein ise layout (columns) ke liye hijack kiya gaya, jiske liye clear/clearfix hacks chahiye the.

Aaj layout ke liye flex/grid hain; float sirf image-text wrapping ke liye reh gaya.
lessons.why: Legacy code padhne ke liye aur interview ke liye: floats ko flow se nikaal dete hain isliye parent ki height 0 ho jati hai. Isko 'collapsing parent' bolte hain.
pros: Text wrapping ke liye ab bhi unique
cons: Layout ke liye fragile aur hacky
gotchas: Float wale children se parent collapse ho jata hai
clear sirf floats par kaam karta hai
Naye layout ke liye float mat use karo — flex/grid

lessons.name: Container Queries
lessons.desc: @container queries size components by their container, not the viewport — true component responsiveness.
lessons.q: How do container queries differ from media queries? Why are they a big deal for design systems?
lessons.qsub: What is a containment context and how do you set one up?
terms: @container (min-width: 400px) — component apne container ki width dekh kar style badalta hai.
Container query units — container width ka 1%.
lessons.what: Definition: Media query viewport dekhti hai; container query component ka apna parent. Parent par container-type: inline-size lagao aur child mein @container likho.
lessons.why: Ek hi card component sidebar (narrow) aur main (wide) dono jagah use hota hai. Media query dono jagah same viewport dekhti hai, container query alag-alag container width. Isse truly reusable components bante hain.
where: card/media object har context mein adapt.
grid mein widget ki width badalti hai.
pros: Media query breakpoints par kam dependency
cons: container-type se element ka size containment aa jata hai (height collapse ho sakti hai)
gotchas: Container khud apne style ko query nahi kar sakta, sirf descendants
inline-size containment ke saath width content se decide nahi hoti
Old browsers ke liye fallback sochna padta hai

lessons.name: Media Queries
lessons.desc: min-width/max-width breakpoints, feature queries, orientation, prefers-color-scheme / reduced-motion.
lessons.q: How do media queries work? What does prefers-reduced-motion let you do?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between min-width and max-width breakpoint strategies?
terms: Viewport width jis par layout badalta hai — content decide kare, device nahi.
Browser support check — media query nahi, feature query.
lessons.what:
Definition: @media conditional CSS hai: viewport width (min-width/max-width), orientation, aur user preferences (dark mode, reduced motion, contrast) ke hisaab se rules lagate hain.

Modern syntax: @media (400px <= width <= 900px).
lessons.why: Responsive design ka base. User preference queries (reduced motion, dark mode) accessibility aur polish ke liye zaroori hain — ye sirf screen size ki baat nahi.
pros: User preferences ko respect karna aasan
cons: Viewport-based hai, component-based nahi (container queries isi ka jawab hain)
gotchas: Breakpoints device names par nahi, content ke toot-ne par rakho
max-width aur min-width mix karne se overlap/gaps ho sakte hain
Hover-only interactions touch par kaam nahi karte — (hover: hover) se guard karo

lessons.name: Mobile-First Strategy
lessons.desc: Base styles for small screens, layer up with min-width; why it produces simpler, faster CSS.
lessons.q: What does mobile-first mean in practice? Why is it preferred over desktop-first?
lessons.qsub: How does mobile-first reduce CSS overrides?
terms: Base CSS chhoti screen ke liye, phir min-width se bade screens par layer.
Basic experience sab ko, behtar features capable devices ko.
Base bade screen ke liye, max-width se chhote par override — zyada overrides.
lessons.what: Definition: Pehle sabse chhoti screen ka layout likho (default CSS, bina media query ke), phir jaise jagah badhe @media (min-width) se complexity add karo.
lessons.why: Mobile par kam CSS parse hota hai aur overrides kam hote hain. Single-column base natural hota hai; usko bade screen par expand karna, desktop layout ko mobile par todne se aasan hai.
cons: Existing desktop-first codebase ko migrate karna kaam hai
gotchas: Mobile-first ka matlab min-width, max-width nahi
Touch targets (≥44px) aur viewport meta mat bhoolo
Base styles mein desktop assumptions (hover, fixed widths) mat daalo

lessons.name: Fluid Type & clamp()
lessons.desc: clamp(min, preferred, max) for fluid font sizes and spacing without breakpoints.
lessons.q: How does clamp() work? Write a fluid font-size that scales between 16px and 24px.
lessons.qsub: Why is clamp() often better than a stack of media queries for typography?
terms: Value ko min aur max ke beech rakhta hai; val viewport ke saath badhta hai.
Font/spacing continuously scale hote hain, breakpoints par jump nahi.
Sirf vw ki font-size zoom ko tod deti hai — rem ke saath mix karo.
lessons.what: Definition: clamp(1rem, 0.8rem + 1vw, 1.5rem) font ko viewport ke saath smoothly scale karta hai, par kabhi 1rem se chhota ya 1.5rem se bada nahi hone deta.
lessons.why: Breakpoints par jump karne wali typography ki jagah ek line se smooth scaling milti hai, aur media queries kam ho jati hain. Spacing ke liye bhi same technique chalti hai.
cons: Values calculate karna thoda tricky (tools madad karte hain)
gotchas: Sirf vw use karne se user zoom kaam nahi karta — rem + vw mix karo
min > max likhoge to min jeetta hai
Bahut bade max se line-length kharab ho sakti hai

lessons.name: Responsive Images (srcset / sizes)
lessons.desc: Serving right-sized images per viewport/DPR, sizes attribute, <picture> for art direction, aspect-ratio.
lessons.q: How do you avoid shipping a 2000px image to a phone? Explain srcset + sizes.
lessons.qsub: How does the aspect-ratio property help prevent layout shift for images?
terms: Browser ko batata hai image layout mein kitni wide dikhegi, taaki wo sahi candidate chune.
aspect-ratio: 16/9 se image load hone se pehle jagah reserve (CLS se bachav).
lessons.what: Definition: srcset + sizes se browser viewport aur DPR ke hisaab se best image chunta hai; <picture> alag crop ya format deta hai; CSS mein max-width:100%; height:auto aur aspect-ratio image ko fluid rakhte hain.
lessons.why: Sahi size ki image LCP aur data dono ke liye bada fayda hai. sizes galat ho to browser galat (badi) image uthata hai — sabse common galti.
lessons.code: img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; } .thumb { aspect-ratio: 1; object-fit: cover; }
cons: Multiple image variants generate/host karne padte hain (CDN/build tool ke bina kaam)
gotchas: sizes viewport width mein nahi, image ki layout width mein soch ke likho
Width/height ya aspect-ratio bina image CLS karti hai
object-fit image ko crop karta hai, stretch nahi

lessons.name: Viewport Units & Mobile Gotchas
lessons.desc: vw/vh/vmin/vmax, the mobile 100vh address-bar problem, dvh/svh/lvh dynamic units.
lessons.q: Why does 100vh behave badly on mobile browsers, and how do dvh/svh fix it?
lessons.qsub: When would you use vmin or vmax?
terms: Small / large / dynamic viewport height — mobile address bar ke hisaab se.
lessons.what:
Definition: vw/vh viewport relative hain. Mobile par address bar scroll par chhupti-dikhti hai to 100vh ek fixed (large) viewport maanta hai aur content bar ke neeche chhup sakta hai.

Fix: dvh (dynamic, bar ke saath badalta), svh (hamesha safe, chhota), lvh (bar hata kar).
lessons.why: Full-screen hero ya bottom-fixed button mobile par 'neeche cut ho raha' wala bug iske wajah se aata hai. Modern solution dvh hai.
cons: dvh se layout address-bar scroll par resize ho sakta hai
gotchas: 100vw vertical scrollbar ko include karta hai — horizontal scroll aa sakta hai
dvh animate/resize ke saath jank de sakta hai; svh safer
Purane browsers ke liye vh fallback pehle likho

lessons.name: Typography Control
lessons.desc: font shorthand, line-height, letter-spacing, font stacks/fallbacks, web-safe fonts, text-wrap: balance.
lessons.q: What makes body text readable? Talk about line-height, measure, and font fallbacks.
lessons.qsub: What does a good font-family fallback stack look like and why?
terms: Unitless value (1.5) best — font-size ke saath scale hoti hai.
Headings ki lines ko barabar balance karta hai (widows kam).
lessons.what: Definition: Readable typography ke levers: font-family stack, font-size, line-height (body text ~1.5), letter-spacing, max-width in ch (45–75 chars), aur text-wrap (balance headings ke liye, pretty paragraphs ke liye).
lessons.why: Typography UI ka 90% hai. Chhoti line-height, bahut lambi lines, ya galat fallback fonts se readability aur CLS dono kharab hoti hain.
cons: Custom fonts load aur layout shift ka trade-off (font-display se manage)
gotchas: line-height: 1.5 unitless rakho — px/em ki line-height inherit galat hoti hai
font shorthand mein font-size aur family dono zaroori hain
Bahut chhoti (<16px) text mobile par zoom trigger kar sakti hai (inputs par)

lessons.name: Overflow & Text Truncation
lessons.desc: overflow visible/hidden/scroll/auto, single-line ellipsis, multi-line line-clamp.
lessons.q: How do you truncate a single line of text with an ellipsis? What about multi-line?
lessons.qsub: Why does text-overflow: ellipsis require white-space and overflow to also be set?
terms: Kata hua text '…' ke saath; nowrap + overflow:hidden ke saath chahiye.
lessons.what: Definition: Single-line ellipsis ke liye teen properties ek saath: white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis. Multi-line ke liye line-clamp.
lessons.why: Cards aur lists mein lambe titles layout todte hain. Truncation sahi karna ek common machine-coding aur interview sawaal hai. Flex children mein min-width:0 bhi chahiye.
cons: Content chhup jata hai — full text tooltip/expand se dena padta hai
gotchas: Flex item mein ellipsis ke liye min-width: 0 zaroori
text-overflow ko overflow (hidden) chahiye
overflow: hidden sticky/box-shadow ko clip kar sakta hai

lessons.name: Pseudo-classes (:hover, :focus, :nth-child)
lessons.desc: State selectors, structural pseudo-classes, :focus-visible vs :focus, :not(), functional pseudo-classes.
lessons.q: What is the difference between :focus and :focus-visible? Why does it matter for accessibility?
lessons.qsub: How would you style every third item in a list?
terms: Focus ring sirf keyboard navigation par — mouse click par nahi.
Exclude karna; :has() parent selector jaisa kaam karta hai.
lessons.what: Definition: Pseudo-classes element ki state ya position select karte hain: :hover, :focus-visible, :checked, :disabled, :nth-child(), :not(), :has().
lessons.why: State styling bina JS ke ho jati hai. :focus-visible accessibility ke liye zaroori hai (outline mat hatao); :has() se 'is card mein image hai to alag layout' jaise parent-based rules ab possible hain.
cons: Zyada complex pseudo-class chains specificity badhati hain
gotchas: :focus mouse click par bhi lagta hai; :focus-visible keyboard par
:nth-child saare siblings gintata hai, sirf same type nahi (:nth-of-type alag hai)
Hover-only UI touch par kaam nahi karta

lessons.name: Pseudo-elements (::before / ::after)
lessons.desc: Generated content, the content property, decorative shapes, icons, and layout tricks.
lessons.q: What is the difference between a pseudo-class and a pseudo-element?
lessons.qsub: Give a practical use of ::before or ::after you have actually used.
terms: Element ke andar ka generated content; content property zaroori hai.
Input placeholder aur selected text ko style karte hain.
Decorative shape ke liye khaali string de ke box banao.
lessons.what: Definition: ::before/::after element ke content se pehle/baad ek virtual child banate hain. Isme content dena zaroori hai (khaali ho to ""). Decorative icons, underline effects, clearfix, overlays me use hote hain.
lessons.why: Extra HTML elements ke bina decoration. Lekin meaningful content (text jo user ko padhna chahiye) pseudo-element mein mat rakho — screen reader aur copy-paste unreliable hain.
cons: JS se access nahi, aur a11y limited
gotchas: content ke bina ::before render hi nahi hota
Pseudo-elements replaced elements (img, input) par kaam nahi karte
Important text pseudo-element mein mat daalo

lessons.name: Backgrounds & Gradients
lessons.desc: background shorthand, multiple backgrounds, linear/radial/conic gradients, background-size/position.
lessons.q: How do you layer multiple backgrounds? What is the difference between cover and contain?
lessons.qsub: How would you create a subtle striped background with a single gradient?
terms: cover (poora bhare, crop ho sakta hai) vs contain (poora dikhe).
Comma se kai layers: background: url(a), linear-gradient(...).
lessons.what: Definition: background shorthand mein color, image, position, size, repeat. Gradients background-image hote hain. Multiple backgrounds upar se neeche stack hote hain (pehla sabse upar).
lessons.why: Gradients aur multiple backgrounds se bina image files ke rich visuals bante hain, jo chhote aur fast hote hain. Text par overlay ke liye gradient + image ka combo common hai.
where: image + dark gradient for text contrast.
cons: Complex gradients likhna aur debug karna kathin
gotchas: Background image par alt text nahi hota — meaningful image ke liye <img> use karo
Shorthand mein size position ke baad / se aata hai
Gradients ko transition nahi kar sakte directly (use @property ya opacity trick)

lessons.name: Borders, Radius & Shadows
lessons.desc: border-radius, box-shadow (inset, spread), drop-shadow filter vs box-shadow, outline vs border.
lessons.q: What is the difference between box-shadow and filter: drop-shadow? When does each matter?
lessons.qsub: Why should you never remove focus outlines without providing an alternative?
terms: x y blur spread color; inset andar ki shadow.
Element ke actual shape (transparent PNG/SVG) ke hisaab se shadow.
Outline layout space nahi leta aur focus ring ke liye hai.
lessons.what: Definition: border-radius corners round karta hai (50% = circle). box-shadow element ke box ke peeche shadow banata hai; multiple shadows comma se. outline border jaisa hai par layout nahi badalta.
lessons.why: Elevation (cards, modals) shadows se dikhai jati hai. Layered soft shadows flat design se behtar depth dete hain. Focus indicator ke liye outline use karo, outline:none nahi.
cons: Badi blur wali shadows paint expensive ho sakti hain animate karne par
gotchas: box-shadow box ke shape par hoti hai, transparent PNG ke shape par nahi (drop-shadow chahiye)
Shadow ko animate karne se repaint hota hai — ::after opacity trick behtar
outline: none bina replacement ke accessibility bug hai

lessons.name: CSS Transitions
lessons.desc: transition-property/duration/timing-function/delay, which properties are animatable, easing curves.
lessons.q: How does a CSS transition work? Which properties are cheap to animate and which are expensive?
lessons.qsub: Why does transition: all can be a performance foot-gun?
terms: Property ki value badalne par smooth interpolation: transition: opacity .2s ease.
Jiski value continuous ho (color, transform, opacity). display normally nahi.
lessons.what: Definition: Transition property ki value ek state se doosri par jaate waqt beech ke frames khud banata hai. Trigger state change se hota hai (hover, class toggle). Syntax: property duration timing-function delay.
lessons.why: Chhote UI feedback (hover, open/close) ke liye JS ki zarurat nahi. Sahi property chunna zaroori hai: transform/opacity smooth rehte hain, width/height layout trigger karte hain.
cons: Sirf do states ke beech; complex sequence ke liye keyframes
gotchas: transition: all se unexpected properties animate hote hain aur perf kharab
display: none → block ko transition nahi hota (ab transition-behavior: allow-discrete / @starting-style se possible)
auto height ko animate nahi kar sakte (grid-template-rows: 0fr→1fr trick use karo)

lessons.name: Keyframe Animations
lessons.desc: @keyframes, animation shorthand, iteration, direction, fill-mode, play-state.
lessons.q: How do @keyframes differ from transitions? When would you reach for each?
lessons.qsub: What does animation-fill-mode: forwards do?
terms: Animation ke steps define karta hai: from/to ya percentages.
forwards = end state rukti hai; backwards = delay mein start state.
lessons.what: Definition: @keyframes name { 0% {...} 100% {...} } se multi-step animation banti hai; element par animation: name 1s ease-in-out infinite alternate lagate hain. Ye trigger ke bina apne aap chal sakti hai.
lessons.why: Loaders, attention pulses, entrance animations jaise sequences transitions se nahi ban paate. Keyframes se multi-step aur looping animations CSS mein ho jati hain.
cons: Dynamic values (JS data) ke saath control kam; Web Animations API behtar
gotchas: animation-fill-mode: both ke bina animation khatam hone par start state par wapas aa jata hai
Reduced-motion users ke liye infinite animations band karo
Same element par animation aur transition conflict kar sakte hain

lessons.name: Transforms (translate / scale / rotate)
lessons.desc: 2D/3D transforms, transform-origin, why transforms do not trigger layout, will-change.
lessons.q: Why is animating transform smoother than animating top/left?
lessons.qsub: What does transform-origin control and when do you change it?
terms: 2D transforms; ab individual properties bhi hain: translate: 10px.
Jis point ke around rotate/scale ho (default center).
Browser ko hint ki ye property badlegi — layer promote ho sakti hai.
lessons.what: Definition: transform element ko visually move/scale/rotate/skew karta hai bina layout badle (doosre elements ki jagah wahi rehti hai). Order matter karta hai: translate() rotate() aur rotate() translate() alag result dete hain.
lessons.why: Transform layout aur paint skip karke seedha compositor par chalta hai, isliye animation smooth (60fps) hoti hai. left/top animate karna layout trigger karta hai — slow.
cons: Naya stacking context + containing block banta hai
gotchas: transform position:fixed ke children ka containing block badal deta hai
Layout space nahi badalti — overlap ho sakta hai
will-change sab par mat lagao, memory kharch hoti hai

lessons.name: Animation Performance (compositor-friendly)
lessons.desc: Animate only transform & opacity to stay on the compositor; avoid layout/paint thrash; will-change budget.
lessons.q: Which two properties can you animate without triggering layout or paint, and why?
lessons.qsub: What does will-change do and why should you use it sparingly?
terms: transform aur opacity main thread ke bina GPU par animate hote hain.
width, top, box-shadow animate karna har frame par layout/paint karwata hai.
Sirf jaha zarurat ho tabhi; bahut layers memory khate hain.
lessons.what: Definition: Smooth animation ke liye sirf transform aur opacity animate karo. Ye properties layout aur paint skip karke compositor par chalti hain, jabki width/height/top/left layout, aur background/box-shadow paint trigger karte hain.
lessons.why: 60fps = 16ms per frame. Layout/paint main thread par hote hain aur JS ke saath compete karte hain; compositor animations JS busy ho tab bhi smooth rehte hain. DevTools Performance panel mein jank dikhta hai.
cons: Layout-based animations (height auto) ke liye workaround chahiye
gotchas: will-change ko permanent mat lagao
Shadow animate karne ke liye ::after ki opacity animate karo
Reduced-motion ko respect karo

lessons.name: Critical Rendering Path
lessons.desc: DOM + CSSOM → render tree → layout → paint → composite; render-blocking CSS/JS; how the browser paints.
lessons.q: Walk me through how the browser turns HTML and CSS into pixels on screen.
lessons.qsub: Why is CSS render-blocking, and how do you reduce that cost?
terms: DOM + CSSOM ka combine; sirf visible nodes.
CSS (aur sync JS) page ka first paint rok dete hain.
Geometry nikalna, pixels bharna, layers ko GPU par jodna.
lessons.what: Definition: Browser HTML se DOM, CSS se CSSOM banata hai, dono se render tree, phir layout (positions/sizes), paint (pixels), composite (layers). CSS render-blocking hai; sync JS parser-blocking aur CSSOM par bhi wait karta hai.
lessons.why: First paint tab hota hai jab render tree ready ho. Critical CSS inline karna, baaki defer/lazy karna, aur defer scripts se FCP/LCP behtar hote hain.
lessons.code:
<head>
  <style>/* critical above-the-fold CSS inline */</style>
  <link rel="preload" href="/fonts/inter.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/app.css" media="print" onload="this.media='all'">
  <script src="/app.js" defer></script>
</head>
where: critical CSS inline for fast FCP.
Lighthouse / DevTools se blocking resources dhoondhna.
pros: Rendering pipeline samajh kar targeted optimization
cons: Critical CSS maintain karna extra tooling maangta hai
gotchas: Sync script CSS download hone tak ruk jata hai
@import CSS waterfall banata hai
Bade CSS file poore page ko block karti hai

lessons.name: Reflow vs Repaint vs Composite
lessons.desc: Layout (reflow) recalculates geometry; paint fills pixels; composite layers GPU-blend. Which props trigger which.
lessons.q: What is the difference between reflow, repaint, and composite? Which is most expensive?
lessons.qsub: Give three property changes that force a reflow and three that only repaint.
terms: Elements ki geometry dobara calculate — mehenga.
Pixels dobara bharna (color/shadow badla, geometry nahi).
Layers ko GPU par jodna — sabse sasta.
lessons.what:
Definition: Property badalne par browser kitna kaam karta hai: layout (width, margin, font-size, top) → paint → composite. Paint-only: color, background, box-shadow. Composite-only: transform, opacity.

Layout badle to paint aur composite bhi hote hain.
lessons.why: Jitni kam stages trigger hon utna sasta. Isliye animations transform/opacity se karte hain aur DOM ko bar-bar read/write nahi karte.
pros: Pipeline samajhna optimization ka base hai
cons: Properties ki list yaad rakhna padta hai (csstriggers jaisi references)
gotchas: Ek chhota layout change poore subtree ko affect kar sakta hai
display:none se layout hat jata hai, visibility:hidden se nahi
JS mein layout properties padhna (offsetHeight) forced reflow trigger karta hai

lessons.name: Layout Thrashing & Batching
lessons.desc: Forced synchronous layout from read-after-write in JS; batching reads then writes; requestAnimationFrame.
lessons.q: What is layout thrashing? How do you avoid forced synchronous layout in a loop?
lessons.qsub: Which DOM reads force a synchronous layout flush?
terms: Style badalne ke turant baad layout property padhna — browser ko layout turant karna padta hai.
Pehle saare reads, phir saare writes.
Visual updates ko next frame se pehle schedule karna.
lessons.what: Definition: Layout thrashing tab hoti hai jab loop mein read (offsetHeight) aur write (style.height = ...) alternate hote hain — har read par browser layout recompute karta hai.
lessons.why: 100 elements ke loop mein 100 layouts ho jate hain; reads batch karne par sirf 1. Ye 'JS se animation/measuring jank karti hai' ka sabse aam kaaran hai.
pros: Bade speedup chhote code change se
cons: Code structure thoda rigid ho jata hai
gotchas: getBoundingClientRect, scrollTop, offsetHeight sab forced layout trigger kar sakte hain
ResizeObserver/IntersectionObserver polling se behtar hain
Frameworks mein bhi effect ke andar read/write mix mat karo

lessons.name: Core Web Vitals (LCP / CLS / INP)
lessons.desc: Largest Contentful Paint, Cumulative Layout Shift, Interaction to Next Paint; targets and common fixes.
lessons.q: What are the Core Web Vitals and what causes a poor score in each?
lessons.qsub: How would you diagnose and fix a high CLS on a page?
terms: Largest Contentful Paint — sabse bada content kab dikha (target ≤ 2.5s).
Cumulative Layout Shift — layout kitna hila (target ≤ 0.1).
Interaction to Next Paint — click/tap ke baad screen kitni jaldi update hui (target ≤ 200ms).
lessons.what:
Definition: Core Web Vitals real-user experience ke 3 metrics hain: LCP (loading), CLS (visual stability), INP (responsiveness; FID ki jagah aaya).

Fixes: LCP image preload/optimize, CLS ke liye image width/height aur font fallback, INP ke liye long tasks todna.
lessons.why: Ye Google search ranking signal bhi hain aur directly conversion se jude hain. Lab data (Lighthouse) aur field data (CrUX) alag ho sakte hain; asli users ka data field wala hai.
lessons.code: /* CLS: jagah reserve */ .ad-slot { min-height: 250px; } img { height: auto; } /* width/height attrs se ratio mil jata hai */ // INP: long task todo await scheduler.yield?.();
where: LCP image aur CLS jaha conversions sensitive hain.
cons: Field data collect karna (RUM) alag effort hai
gotchas: LCP image par lazy-loading mat lagao
Late-loading ads/banners/fonts CLS badhate hain
Lab score acha ho par field INP kharab ho sakta hai

lessons.name: Web Font Loading (FOUT / FOIT)
lessons.desc: font-display swap/optional, preloading fonts, fallback metrics, layout shift from font swaps.
lessons.q: What is the difference between FOUT and FOIT? How does font-display control it?
lessons.qsub: How do you prevent a layout shift when a web font finishes loading?
terms: Flash of Unstyled Text — fallback font dikhta hai, phir swap.
Flash of Invisible Text — font aane tak text chhupta hai.
lessons.what: Definition: Web font load hone tak browser text ko ya to chhupata hai (FOIT) ya fallback se dikhata hai (FOUT). font-display: swap fallback turant dikhata hai aur font aane par swap karta hai; optional sirf cache mein ho to use karta hai (shift nahi).
lessons.why: Font swap se text ki width badalti hai aur layout shift (CLS) hota hai. Preload + size-adjusted fallback (size-adjust, ascent-override) se shift kam hota hai.
pros: Text jaldi dikhta hai, shift kam
cons: Perfect fallback metrics nikalna thoda kaam hai
gotchas: Font preload mein crossorigin zaroori hai warna do baar download
Bahut zyada weights/variants load mat karo
Variable fonts file size bachate hain

lessons.name: CSS Containment & content-visibility
lessons.desc: contain property, content-visibility: auto to skip offscreen rendering, performance isolation.
lessons.q: What does content-visibility: auto do for a long page?
lessons.qsub: What kinds of containment does the contain property offer?
terms: Browser ko batana ki subtree ke changes bahar affect nahi karte: layout, paint, size, style.
Offscreen content ka rendering skip, scroll par render.
Skip kiye hue content ki placeholder size (scrollbar jump rokne ke liye).
lessons.what: Definition: contain se browser ko hint milta hai ki element ke andar ke changes bahar layout/paint ko affect nahi karenge, to wo kaam ko isolate kar sakta hai. content-visibility: auto offscreen sections ka layout/paint skip kar deta hai.
lessons.why: Lambe pages (feeds, articles) mein initial render time bahut kam ho sakta hai. Bina contain-intrinsic-size ke skip kiye hue content ki height 0 hoti hai aur scrollbar jump karta hai.
pros: Initial render aur scroll cost kam
cons: Galat intrinsic size se scrollbar jump
gotchas: contain: size element ki size content se nahi nikalne deta — explicit size do
content-visibility skip kiye content ko find-in-page mein dikhata hai par accessibility tree mein rehta hai
Isse sab par lagane se pehle measure karo

lessons.name: Naming Methodologies (BEM)
lessons.desc: BEM block__element--modifier, why naming conventions fight specificity and scale in large codebases.
lessons.q: What problem does BEM solve? How does it keep specificity flat?
lessons.qsub: What are the trade-offs of BEM versus utility-first CSS?
lessons.what: Definition: BEM (Block__Element--Modifier) ek naming convention hai: .block__element--modifier. Isse class ka naam hi batata hai ki wo kis component ka hissa hai.
lessons.why: Global CSS mein naam collision aur specificity wars hote hain. BEM flat, ek-class selectors deta hai jo same specificity par rehte hain, isliye override predictable hota hai. Nuksaan: lambe class names.
lessons.code:
Title

.card { padding: 16px; } .card--featured { border: 2px solid gold; } .card__title { font-size: 1.25rem; } .card__btn--primary { background: royalblue; }
pros: Naam dekhkar structure samajh aata hai
cons: Verbose class names
Nesting deep ho to naam bahut lambe
gotchas: .card__title__link jaisa nesting mat banao — flatten karo
Modifier akele nahi, base class ke saath lagta hai (card card--featured)
Scoped CSS (modules) ke saath BEM aksar zaruri nahi

lessons.name: CSS Modules & Scoping
lessons.desc: Locally scoped class names, hashing, composition; solving the global namespace problem.
lessons.q: How do CSS Modules prevent class-name collisions? What does the build step do?
lessons.qsub: How does composes work in CSS Modules?
terms: Class names file ke andar local; build tool unhe unique hash banata hai.
Ek class mein doosri class ke styles reuse karna.
lessons.what: Definition: *.module.css file import karne par har class name ek unique generated name ban jata hai (card_3xK9a), isliye collision possible nahi. Aap styles.card se use karte ho.
lessons.why: Global namespace problem hal ho jata hai bina runtime cost ke (static CSS file). Plain CSS ka sab kuch milta hai: media queries, pseudo-classes, tools. Dynamic values ke liye CSS variables use hote hain.
cons: Dynamic styling (props-based) ke liye CSS variables ya inline style chahiye
Naming conventions ab bhi zaroori (e.g. state classes)
gotchas: Global selectors (body, [data-theme]) ko :global chahiye
Class names dynamic strings se nahi bante — styles['x'] use karo
Child component ke styles override karna difficult (CSS variables se)

lessons.name: CSS-in-JS (styled-components / emotion)
lessons.desc: Runtime vs zero-runtime CSS-in-JS, dynamic styling from props, SSR concerns, performance trade-offs.
lessons.q: What are the pros and cons of CSS-in-JS? What is the runtime cost?
lessons.qsub: Why have zero-runtime solutions (Linaria, vanilla-extract) gained popularity?
terms: styled-components/emotion: JS mein styles, runtime par CSS inject hota hai.
Linaria/vanilla-extract/Panda: build time par static CSS.
Component ke props se dynamic styles.
lessons.what: Definition: CSS-in-JS styles ko component ke saath JS mein likhta hai (template literals ya objects). Runtime libraries render ke dauran CSS inject karti hain; zero-runtime tools build time par static CSS nikaal dete hain.
lessons.why: Colocation, dynamic styling aur automatic scoping milte hain. Nuksaan: runtime overhead, SSR/streaming complexity aur React Server Components ke saath dikkat — isliye industry zero-runtime ya CSS Modules/Tailwind ki taraf shift hui.
cons: Runtime cost aur bundle size
RSC / streaming SSR ke saath friction
gotchas: Component render mein styled() define mat karo — har render naya class banata hai
SSR mein style flash (FOUC) ke liye extra setup
Props DOM tak leak na ho (transient $prop use karo)

lessons.name: Utility-First CSS (Tailwind)
lessons.desc: Utility classes, design tokens via config, purge/JIT, when utility-first helps or hurts maintainability.
lessons.q: What is the case for and against Tailwind / utility-first CSS?
lessons.qsub: How does Tailwind keep the shipped CSS small?
terms: Spacing/colors config mein tay; utilities unse bante hain.
Sirf use hui classes ka CSS generate hota hai.
lessons.what: Definition: Utility-first (Tailwind) mein HTML par chhoti single-purpose classes lagake style karte hain, custom CSS likhne ke bajay. Config (theme tokens) se consistent spacing/colors milte hain.
lessons.why: Naming ki zarurat nahi, dead CSS nahi, aur design system enforced. Nuksaan: lambe class strings aur component extraction ki discipline chahiye (React component se reuse, @apply se nahi).
lessons.code:
<button class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-4 py-2
  text-white hover:bg-blue-700 focus-visible:outline-2 md:px-6">
  Save
</button>

// tailwind.config
theme: { extend: { colors: { brand: '#0a84ff' } } }
cons: Cluttered markup
Team ko conventions seekhne padte hain
gotchas: Dynamic class names (bg-${color}-500) purge ho jati hain — full class names likho
Bahut lambe class lists ko component mein extract karo
Arbitrary values ka overuse design tokens tod deta hai

lessons.name: Design Tokens & Theming (dark mode)
lessons.desc: Token layers, CSS variables for theming, prefers-color-scheme, per-component theming without JS.
lessons.q: How would you architect a themeable design system that supports light/dark and brand themes?
lessons.qsub: Why are CSS variables better than duplicated stylesheets for theming?
lessons.what: Definition: Tokens ko do layers mein rakho: primitive (--blue-600) aur semantic (--color-primary: var(--blue-600)). Theme badalna matlab semantic tokens ko re-map karna; components sirf semantic tokens use karte hain.
lessons.why: Dark mode, brand themes aur high-contrast sab CSS variables ke override se bina JS rewrite ke ho jate hain. color-scheme property native controls (scrollbar, inputs) ko bhi theme karti hai.
cons: Token naming aur governance discipline chahiye
gotchas: Flash of wrong theme: theme attribute HTML load se pehle set karo (inline script)
Contrast ratios dono themes mein check karo
Components mein raw hex mat likho — tokens use karo

lessons.name: Preprocessors (Sass) & @layer
lessons.desc: Sass nesting/mixins/functions, native CSS nesting, cascade layers (@layer) for predictable ordering.
lessons.q: What do preprocessors still offer now that CSS has variables and nesting?
lessons.qsub: What problem do CSS cascade layers (@layer) solve?
terms: Variables, nesting, mixins, functions — compile hoke CSS banta hai.
Cascade layers: pehle declare kiye layers ka order specificity se upar hota hai.
lessons.what:
Definition: Sass jaise preprocessors CSS ko features dete the jo native nahi the (variables, nesting, mixins). Aaj CSS variables, nesting, @layer, color-mix() native ho gaye hain, isliye preprocessor ki zarurat kam hai.

@layer reset, base, components, utilities; se ordering specificity ke bajay layer order se tay hoti hai.
lessons.why: Cascade layers specificity wars ka structural solution hain: third-party CSS ko neeche ki layer mein rakho aur apni styles ooper — bina !important ke override ho jati hain.
cons: Unlayered styles layered styles se hamesha upar hote hain — confusing
gotchas: Layer ka order pehli declaration se tay hota hai
!important mein layer order ulta ho jata hai
Sass mixins/functions ke bina kuch cheezein ab bhi native nahi
